sections.title: Eligibility and preparation
sections.text:
Eligibility for your route [Standing rule]
Eligible in principle for the Mathematics PhD with a UChicago mathematics bachelor's completed before
enrollment. A mathematics degree is recommended, or comparably strong preparation; normally GPA 3.0 or
better. A year each of upper-division algebra and real analysis is encouraged. Admission is departmental, with
no published requirement to secure an adviser first. International F1 applicants are accepted. [s1] [s8] [s7]
Before submission [Standing rule]
Choose Mathematics PhD in the online application; UCSD permits only one application to a program within a
department, so do not also submit the mathematics MA/MS application. Prepare unofficial records, SOP, a list of
mathematics courses already taken and projected with textbooks, and at least three referees. Arrange official
test delivery if submitting scores. No interview or advance faculty commitment is required by the public
mathematics process. [s1] [s10] [s2]
Adviser contact [Standing rule]
No faculty sponsorship is required to apply. The department says applicants can arrange a faculty conversation
themselves when there is a specific reason, while respecting faculty time. Application questions:
mathgradadmissions@ucsd.edu (the FAQ also prints mathgradadmissions@math.ucsd.edu). Faculty listed
below are research fits; none is confirmed to recruit for 2027. [s2] [s1]
Portal workflow [Standing rule]
Use the UCSD graduate application and upload materials electronically; mathematics does not want mailed
application documents. Track submitted status and recommendation receipt in the portal. Some
postsubmission uploads such as transcripts/CV/miscellaneous samples are allowed centrally, but late review is

not guaranteed. Official admission is communicated through the portal/email. After accepting, complete the
decision reply, legal-residence form and international I-20/financial-document process. [s10] [s2] [s9] [s17]
Cycle verification [2027 confirmed]
The mathematics page explicitly announces fall-2027 opening and December 2, 2026 PhD deadline. Most
central procedural policies are standing. Contract salary rates for October 2027 are explicit; the department's
exact stipend and summer offer are not. Some admitted-student credential dates remain fall-2026 examples.
[s1] [s19] [s9]

sections.title: Deadlines by stage
sections.text:
Academic application [2027 confirmed]
Fall 2027 Mathematics PhD: opens September 2, 2026; closes December 2, 2026. The same deadline applies to
the listed mathematics PhD variants including CSME/statistics; separate mathematics master's programs close
February 3, 2027. The checked mathematics page does not state a closing clock/time zone. Late applications
are not accepted. [s1] [s2]
Funding consideration [2027 confirmed]
No separate first-year departmental funding application deadline is stated; submit the PhD admission
application by December 2, 2026 for the ordinary support process. Fellowship nomination deadlines and extra
forms depend on the award and must be confirmed separately. [s1] [s3] [s14]
Reference receipt [2027 confirmed]
Target December 2, 2026. The mathematics FAQ explicitly says it continues PhD review in January and
February as letters arrive, but gives no final late-letter cutoff. Central admissions permits postdeadline uploads
without guaranteeing review. This is not a blanket extension of the applicant's December 2 submission
deadline. [s1] [s2] [s6]
Test-score receipt [Standing rule]
Submit relevant scores with the December 2 file; no distinct 2027 score-arrival grace deadline was found.
Mathematics recommends taking the Math Subject GRE no later than October to have scores ready. Official
ETS delivery uses institution 4836 with no department code; central processing normally takes 5-7 business
days after receipt. Both GREs are optional, but the mathematics test is highly recommended. [s2] [s16]
Supporting documents [2027 confirmed]
Upload application records, SOP and the required course/textbook list by December 2, 2026. After provisional
admission, official final records are required to finalize admission; the checked admitted-student page's May 15
credential date is labeled fall 2026 and must not be silently reused for 2027. Use the 2027 offer/checklist for
the exact official-record deadline. [s1] [s7] [s9]
Accepting an offer [Standing rule]
Standing central policy: students admitted by March 15 generally reply by April 15; those admitted after March
30 receive at least three weeks from the offer date. The page does not fill the March 16-30 interval with a
universal rule. Confirm the actual 2027 offer deadline. Complete the Statement of Legal Residence within two
weeks after accepting. [s8] [s9]

sections.title: English and GRE
sections.text:
English requirement [Conflict]
Current central minimums if not exempt: TOEFL 4.5 on the revised scale or 85 on the previous scale, IELTS 7,
PTE Academic 65, or DET 120; scores normally valid two years. DET is accepted from the fall-2026 cycle.
Mathematics also recommends strong speaking performance. The mathematics FAQ retains an older
one-year-study exemption formulation and older TOEFL scale; the current central degree-and-GPA rule should
be checked when recording an exemption. [s4] [s2]

UChicago English exemption [Standing rule]
The current central policy exempts an applicant who has earned or will earn a bachelor's, master's or doctorate
with at least B/3.0 grades from a regionally accredited US institution where English is the sole instructional
language. A UChicago bachelor's therefore qualifies conditionally on those academic facts. The current TA
policy explicitly accepts this qualifying prior-degree admission exemption for teaching certification as well;
ensure the completed degree and exemption are recorded before the first TA appointment. [s4] [s5]
GRE General [Standing rule]
Not required. Public mathematics wording permits optional submission; it does not say scores are forbidden or
ignored. [s1] [s2]
GRE Mathematics [Standing rule]
Not required, but highly recommended. No departmental minimum score is published, and the overall
application is reviewed holistically. [s1] [s2]

sections.title: Academic records
sections.text:
Transcripts and degree records [Standing rule]
At application, scan transcripts from every institution attended after high school. Include front and back even if
the back is blank, current name/institution/attendance dates, grades, credits, grading key and any degree
conferral. If unavailable, upload an explanation. Do not send official hard copies before admission. Official final
records and relevant translations follow provisional admission. The mandatory WES ICAP or TEC
course-by-course evaluation applies to admitted students with degrees earned outside the US, not to the
UChicago degree itself. [s7]
Mathematics-course list [Standing rule]
A list of mathematics courses taken and projected, including textbooks used, is explicitly required. The public
page does not specify a template or a word/page limit. [s1]
Course descriptions [Unresolved]
Textbooks are explicitly requested with the course list; separate syllabi or full course descriptions are not listed
publicly. Check the live upload instructions before adding them. [s1]

sections.title: Recommendation letters
sections.text:
Number and type [Standing rule]
At least three recommendations. Central admissions permits more in principle but advises checking with the
department before exceeding the requested number. [s1] [s6]
Scholarship references [Standing rule]
No extra reference is published for the standard entrance assistantship. Award-specific nominations may differ.
As a later, continuing-student example, Friends of the International Center requires one faculty
recommendation endorsed by the chair; it is not a first-year admission requirement. [s1] [s14]
What sends the invitation [Unresolved]
The central FAQ documents electronic requests, resends and new requests, but does not establish the exact
mathematics-portal click that sends the first invitation. Verify the confirmation screen rather than assuming
that typing a name immediately emails the referee. [s6]
Before versus after submission [Unresolved]
Application submission does not require all letters already to be complete, and writers can upload afterward.
Request management exists in the application; the public mathematics/central instructions do not explicitly
establish whether a first invitation is automatically held until final submission. Arrange requests early and
inspect their sent status. [s6]

Receipt confirmation [Standing rule]
The application portal shows each recommendation's status and allows reminder/new requests. The request
email supplies the application deadline. Central admissions accepts Interfolio using the service's generated
recommender email address. [s6]
Updating and reusing letters [Standing rule]
Before final submission, referee information can be edited; afterward the portal permits some
personal-information edits, reminders and exclusion. Recommender email addresses and the Buckley/FERPA
waiver cannot be changed through that edit. A writer's ability to replace a submitted letter, and reuse across
cycles/programs, are not publicly settled. [s6]

sections.text:
Academic CV / resume [Unresolved]
A CV is not explicitly included in the mathematics required-materials list checked. Central application help
allows CV/resume uploads or updates, but that does not establish a mathematics requirement, limit or promise
of review. Inspect the live mathematics form before preparing a final upload. [s1] [s10]
Statement of purpose [Standing rule]
SOP is required. The central prompt asks, in paraphrase, how your interests developed; preparation through
research, study/work/service and lessons learned; degree/subfield and career goals; one or two possible
research directions; and fit with UCSD faculty. It also invites relevant qualities, initiative, independence and
educational barriers. No public mathematics-specific word/page, font or margin limit was found. Upload
through the application; the linked source preserves the full wording. [s1] [s11]

sections.title: Funding and fees
sections.text:
Amount and coverage [2027 confirmed]
The department does not publish an exact guaranteed 2027 annual package. For a UCSD Group-1
quarter-system TA at 50% FTE, the signed UC wage table explicitly sets October 1, 2027 monthly salary points
at $4,278, $4,449 and $4,582. A nine-month point-1 appointment would total $38,502 gross (9 × $4,278;
calculation, not an offer). October 2026 point 1 is $4,100. Tuition/fee remission and qualifying health-premium
coverage are additional benefits governed by appointment and contract; summer pay is separate. [s19] [s3] [s20]
[s21]
Years of support [Standing rule]
The mathematics department typically supports PhD students for up to five academic years, explicitly October
through June, with teaching appointments and tuition/fee support. This is conditional on satisfactory progress,
teaching performance and available funding. No universal summer or twelve-month funding guarantee is
stated. Mathematics master's students have no comparable funding guarantee. [s3] [s1]
International eligibility [Standing rule]
International PhD students can receive department TA/GSR/fellowship support. Record the admission-English
exemption and satisfy TA certification before teaching. Verify nonresident supplemental tuition coverage
explicitly: the UC agreement's automatic postcandidacy NRST reduction/remission has a limited three-year
period and is not a substitute for an offer's precandidacy funding commitment. [s3] [s5] [s20]
Conditions and duties [Standing rule]
Normal campus academic-year employment maximum is 50%/20 hours weekly; 50% appointments require 12
units, good standing, GPA 3.0 and satisfactory degree progress within support/time limits. More than eight
accumulated F/U units is disqualifying under the checked support policy. TA/Associate service is capped at 18
quarters. Qualifying appointments of at least 25% receive contractual tuition/student-services/campus-fee
remission and health-premium benefits, with individual exclusions/cost-sharing to confirm. Summer
appointments may reach 100% where permitted and are not promised. [s15] [s20] [s21]
Extra funding application [Standing rule]
Ordinary departmental support is part of PhD admissions consideration. Competitive fellowships may require
departmental nomination and award-specific materials; confirm these with the graduate coordinator. No
universal additional entrance funding form is published. [s3] [s13] [s14]
Other funding routes [Standing rule]
GSR appointments depend on adviser grants; fellowships and summer teaching/research may supplement
support. Central internal opportunities communicate current amounts/eligibility through nomination calls. The
undated department page describes San Diego/Cota-Robles awards of up to $20,000 annually, but current
names, amounts, citizenship rules and availability require verification. Later FIC awards are open to all
nationalities after candidacy, typically about $2,000 with a December call; dissertation awards and narrowly
restricted external fellowships have separate eligibility. None is guaranteed to an entering F1 applicant. [s3]
[s13] [s14]
Application fee [Standing rule]
International application fee $155; US citizens/permanent residents $135. John's F1 status places him in the
international fee category. [s1] [s12]

Fee waiver [Standing rule]
The central waiver is restricted to eligible US citizens/permanent residents; no mathematics exception for
international applicants was found. Eligible domestic requests should be filed at least one week before the
program deadline, with required current documentation; November 25, 2026 is the arithmetic one-week
planning date for a December 2 deadline, not an independently announced international waiver route. [s12]

University of California, San Diego
United States · Mathematics PhD

materials · Funding and fees · Conflicts and remaining checks · Faculty · Sources
Pay attention to
• December 2, 2026 is the explicit PhD deadline; the master's February 3 date does not apply.
• Math Subject GRE is optional but highly recommended; General GRE is optional.
• UChicago degree/GPA can meet both admission and current TA English exemptions; confirm the recorded
exemption.
• Course list must include projected courses and textbooks.
• References can arrive during January/February review, but there is no published final grace cutoff or
guaranteed late review.
• The $38,502 calculation assumes nine months at the October 2027 50% point-1 TA rate; summer and the
actual offer remain unconfirmed.
• Wenzl and Rabin are emeriti; DeVleming and Zhang are current UCSD faculty despite older institutions'
pages.
• McKernan's current 2026 research is verified through a departmental talk, but a recent paper was not
established; his listed 2018 paper is explicitly historical.
Eligibility and preparation
Eligibility for your route [Standing rule]
Eligible in principle for the Mathematics PhD with a UChicago mathematics bachelor's completed before
enrollment. A mathematics degree is recommended, or comparably strong preparation; normally GPA 3.0 or
better. A year each of upper-division algebra and real analysis is encouraged. Admission is departmental, with
no published requirement to secure an adviser first. International F1 applicants are accepted. [s1] [s8] [s7]
Before submission [Standing rule]
Choose Mathematics PhD in the online application; UCSD permits only one application to a program within a
department, so do not also submit the mathematics MA/MS application. Prepare unofficial records, SOP, a list of
mathematics courses already taken and projected with textbooks, and at least three referees. Arrange official
test delivery if submitting scores. No interview or advance faculty commitment is required by the public
mathematics process. [s1] [s10] [s2]
Adviser contact [Standing rule]
No faculty sponsorship is required to apply. The department says applicants can arrange a faculty conversation
themselves when there is a specific reason, while respecting faculty time. Application questions:
mathgradadmissions@ucsd.edu (the FAQ also prints mathgradadmissions@math.ucsd.edu). Faculty listed
below are research fits; none is confirmed to recruit for 2027. [s2] [s1]
Portal workflow [Standing rule]
Use the UCSD graduate application and upload materials electronically; mathematics does not want mailed
application documents. Track submitted status and recommendation receipt in the portal. Some
postsubmission uploads such as transcripts/CV/miscellaneous samples are allowed centrally, but late review is

not guaranteed. Official admission is communicated through the portal/email. After accepting, complete the
decision reply, legal-residence form and international I-20/financial-document process. [s10] [s2] [s9] [s17]
Cycle verification [2027 confirmed]
The mathematics page explicitly announces fall-2027 opening and December 2, 2026 PhD deadline. Most
central procedural policies are standing. Contract salary rates for October 2027 are explicit; the department's
exact stipend and summer offer are not. Some admitted-student credential dates remain fall-2026 examples.
[s1] [s19] [s9]
Deadlines by stage
Academic application [2027 confirmed]
Fall 2027 Mathematics PhD: opens September 2, 2026; closes December 2, 2026. The same deadline applies to
the listed mathematics PhD variants including CSME/statistics; separate mathematics master's programs close
February 3, 2027. The checked mathematics page does not state a closing clock/time zone. Late applications
are not accepted. [s1] [s2]
Funding consideration [2027 confirmed]
No separate first-year departmental funding application deadline is stated; submit the PhD admission
application by December 2, 2026 for the ordinary support process. Fellowship nomination deadlines and extra
forms depend on the award and must be confirmed separately. [s1] [s3] [s14]
Reference receipt [2027 confirmed]
Target December 2, 2026. The mathematics FAQ explicitly says it continues PhD review in January and
February as letters arrive, but gives no final late-letter cutoff. Central admissions permits postdeadline uploads
without guaranteeing review. This is not a blanket extension of the applicant's December 2 submission
deadline. [s1] [s2] [s6]
Test-score receipt [Standing rule]
Submit relevant scores with the December 2 file; no distinct 2027 score-arrival grace deadline was found.
Mathematics recommends taking the Math Subject GRE no later than October to have scores ready. Official
ETS delivery uses institution 4836 with no department code; central processing normally takes 5-7 business
days after receipt. Both GREs are optional, but the mathematics test is highly recommended. [s2] [s16]
Supporting documents [2027 confirmed]
Upload application records, SOP and the required course/textbook list by December 2, 2026. After provisional
admission, official final records are required to finalize admission; the checked admitted-student page's May 15
credential date is labeled fall 2026 and must not be silently reused for 2027. Use the 2027 offer/checklist for
the exact official-record deadline. [s1] [s7] [s9]
Accepting an offer [Standing rule]
Standing central policy: students admitted by March 15 generally reply by April 15; those admitted after March
30 receive at least three weeks from the offer date. The page does not fill the March 16-30 interval with a
universal rule. Confirm the actual 2027 offer deadline. Complete the Statement of Legal Residence within two
weeks after accepting. [s8] [s9]
English and GRE
English requirement [Conflict]
Current central minimums if not exempt: TOEFL 4.5 on the revised scale or 85 on the previous scale, IELTS 7,
PTE Academic 65, or DET 120; scores normally valid two years. DET is accepted from the fall-2026 cycle.
Mathematics also recommends strong speaking performance. The mathematics FAQ retains an older
one-year-study exemption formulation and older TOEFL scale; the current central degree-and-GPA rule should
be checked when recording an exemption. [s4] [s2]

UChicago English exemption [Standing rule]
The current central policy exempts an applicant who has earned or will earn a bachelor's, master's or doctorate
with at least B/3.0 grades from a regionally accredited US institution where English is the sole instructional
language. A UChicago bachelor's therefore qualifies conditionally on those academic facts. The current TA
policy explicitly accepts this qualifying prior-degree admission exemption for teaching certification as well;
ensure the completed degree and exemption are recorded before the first TA appointment. [s4] [s5]
GRE General [Standing rule]
Not required. Public mathematics wording permits optional submission; it does not say scores are forbidden or
ignored. [s1] [s2]
GRE Mathematics [Standing rule]
Not required, but highly recommended. No departmental minimum score is published, and the overall
application is reviewed holistically. [s1] [s2]
Academic records
Transcripts and degree records [Standing rule]
At application, scan transcripts from every institution attended after high school. Include front and back even if
the back is blank, current name/institution/attendance dates, grades, credits, grading key and any degree
conferral. If unavailable, upload an explanation. Do not send official hard copies before admission. Official final
records and relevant translations follow provisional admission. The mandatory WES ICAP or TEC
course-by-course evaluation applies to admitted students with degrees earned outside the US, not to the
UChicago degree itself. [s7]
Mathematics-course list [Standing rule]
A list of mathematics courses taken and projected, including textbooks used, is explicitly required. The public
page does not specify a template or a word/page limit. [s1]
Course descriptions [Unresolved]
Textbooks are explicitly requested with the course list; separate syllabi or full course descriptions are not listed
publicly. Check the live upload instructions before adding them. [s1]
Recommendation letters
Number and type [Standing rule]
At least three recommendations. Central admissions permits more in principle but advises checking with the
department before exceeding the requested number. [s1] [s6]
Scholarship references [Standing rule]
No extra reference is published for the standard entrance assistantship. Award-specific nominations may differ.
As a later, continuing-student example, Friends of the International Center requires one faculty
recommendation endorsed by the chair; it is not a first-year admission requirement. [s1] [s14]
What sends the invitation [Unresolved]
The central FAQ documents electronic requests, resends and new requests, but does not establish the exact
mathematics-portal click that sends the first invitation. Verify the confirmation screen rather than assuming
that typing a name immediately emails the referee. [s6]
Before versus after submission [Unresolved]
Application submission does not require all letters already to be complete, and writers can upload afterward.
Request management exists in the application; the public mathematics/central instructions do not explicitly
establish whether a first invitation is automatically held until final submission. Arrange requests early and
inspect their sent status. [s6]

Receipt confirmation [Standing rule]
The application portal shows each recommendation's status and allows reminder/new requests. The request
email supplies the application deadline. Central admissions accepts Interfolio using the service's generated
recommender email address. [s6]
Updating and reusing letters [Standing rule]
Before final submission, referee information can be edited; afterward the portal permits some
personal-information edits, reminders and exclusion. Recommender email addresses and the Buckley/FERPA
waiver cannot be changed through that edit. A writer's ability to replace a submitted letter, and reuse across
cycles/programs, are not publicly settled. [s6]
Written materials
Academic CV / resume [Unresolved]
A CV is not explicitly included in the mathematics required-materials list checked. Central application help
allows CV/resume uploads or updates, but that does not establish a mathematics requirement, limit or promise
of review. Inspect the live mathematics form before preparing a final upload. [s1] [s10]
Statement of purpose [Standing rule]
SOP is required. The central prompt asks, in paraphrase, how your interests developed; preparation through
research, study/work/service and lessons learned; degree/subfield and career goals; one or two possible
research directions; and fit with UCSD faculty. It also invites relevant qualities, initiative, independence and
educational barriers. No public mathematics-specific word/page, font or margin limit was found. Upload
through the application; the linked source preserves the full wording. [s1] [s11]
Personal / background statement [Unresolved]
No separate personal/background statement is publicly listed for Mathematics. Personal qualities and relevant
barriers can be addressed within the central SOP guidance. Confirm any live-portal or nomination-specific
additional prompt. [s1] [s11]
Research-interest statement [Standing rule]
Research interests and faculty fit are part of the SOP. Central guidance asks for one or two topics and
expressly recognizes that initial interests may change; no standalone research-interest document is listed. [s11]
Research proposal [Unresolved]
A formal research proposal is not listed among the public Mathematics requirements. The SOP's tentative
research interests do not establish a requirement for a detailed proposal. [s1] [s11]
Writing sample / thesis / research summary [Unresolved]
No thesis, writing sample or full research paper is listed as a required mathematics attachment. Central portal
help allows miscellaneous/writing-sample uploads or updates, but mathematics-specific permission, limits and
whether to upload or link optional papers are unverified. [s1] [s10]
Publications list [Unresolved]
No separate publication-list requirement is published. Research/publications can inform the SOP; permission to
submit full papers, and upload-versus-link preference, are not established. [s1] [s11]
Course-list document [Standing rule]
Required separate list of completed and projected mathematics courses with textbooks. No public format,
length or sample template was established. [s1]
Scholarship essays [Unresolved]
Entrance fellowship essays and nomination prompts are not uniformly public. The department's undated San
Diego/Cota-Robles descriptions should not be treated as an announced 2027 competition. For later FIC support,
the central page asks for a two-page statement covering qualifications/research/career/need/community and

international understanding plus intended use, a CV, unofficial transcript and one endorsed faculty reference;
this is a continuing postcandidacy opportunity. [s13] [s14]
Other short answers / materials [Unresolved]
No further mathematics-specific written document is publicly listed beyond the SOP, records and
course/textbook list. Complete all conditional portal questions and confirm any fellowship-specific short
answers before drafting. [s1] [s10]
Funding and fees
Amount and coverage [2027 confirmed]
The department does not publish an exact guaranteed 2027 annual package. For a UCSD Group-1
quarter-system TA at 50% FTE, the signed UC wage table explicitly sets October 1, 2027 monthly salary points
at $4,278, $4,449 and $4,582. A nine-month point-1 appointment would total $38,502 gross (9 × $4,278;
calculation, not an offer). October 2026 point 1 is $4,100. Tuition/fee remission and qualifying health-premium
coverage are additional benefits governed by appointment and contract; summer pay is separate. [s19] [s3] [s20]
[s21]
Years of support [Standing rule]
The mathematics department typically supports PhD students for up to five academic years, explicitly October
through June, with teaching appointments and tuition/fee support. This is conditional on satisfactory progress,
teaching performance and available funding. No universal summer or twelve-month funding guarantee is
stated. Mathematics master's students have no comparable funding guarantee. [s3] [s1]
International eligibility [Standing rule]
International PhD students can receive department TA/GSR/fellowship support. Record the admission-English
exemption and satisfy TA certification before teaching. Verify nonresident supplemental tuition coverage
explicitly: the UC agreement's automatic postcandidacy NRST reduction/remission has a limited three-year
period and is not a substitute for an offer's precandidacy funding commitment. [s3] [s5] [s20]
Conditions and duties [Standing rule]
Normal campus academic-year employment maximum is 50%/20 hours weekly; 50% appointments require 12
units, good standing, GPA 3.0 and satisfactory degree progress within support/time limits. More than eight
accumulated F/U units is disqualifying under the checked support policy. TA/Associate service is capped at 18
quarters. Qualifying appointments of at least 25% receive contractual tuition/student-services/campus-fee
remission and health-premium benefits, with individual exclusions/cost-sharing to confirm. Summer
appointments may reach 100% where permitted and are not promised. [s15] [s20] [s21]
Extra funding application [Standing rule]
Ordinary departmental support is part of PhD admissions consideration. Competitive fellowships may require
departmental nomination and award-specific materials; confirm these with the graduate coordinator. No
universal additional entrance funding form is published. [s3] [s13] [s14]
Other funding routes [Standing rule]
GSR appointments depend on adviser grants; fellowships and summer teaching/research may supplement
support. Central internal opportunities communicate current amounts/eligibility through nomination calls. The
undated department page describes San Diego/Cota-Robles awards of up to $20,000 annually, but current
names, amounts, citizenship rules and availability require verification. Later FIC awards are open to all
nationalities after candidacy, typically about $2,000 with a December call; dissertation awards and narrowly
restricted external fellowships have separate eligibility. None is guaranteed to an entering F1 applicant. [s3]
[s13] [s14]
Application fee [Standing rule]
International application fee $155; US citizens/permanent residents $135. John's F1 status places him in the
international fee category. [s1] [s12]

Fee waiver [Standing rule]
The central waiver is restricted to eligible US citizens/permanent residents; no mathematics exception for
international applicants was found. Eligible domestic requests should be filed at least one week before the
program deadline, with required current documentation; November 25, 2026 is the arithmetic one-week
planning date for a December 2 deadline, not an independently announced international waiver route. [s12]
